sentences.text: 1  For Petitioner : Mr.S.Subbiah, Senior Counsel   Mr.P.Raja.

For Respondents : Mr.A.Selvendran,
 Special Government Pleader
(For  ORDER (Judgement of the Court was delivered by S.M.Subramaniam J.)
The Review Application has been filed against the order dated 16.07.2012 passed in W.P.No.791 of 2012 on the file of this Court.
2. The learned Senior Counsel Mr.S.Subbiah, appearing on behalf of the petitioner would contend that the land acquired are encroached upon by few persons.
The Government has not utilised the land for the purpose for which the lands were acquired from the land owners.
Thus, the petitioner is entitled to seek reconveyance of land under Section 48(B) of the Land Acquisition Act.
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis Review Application No.192 of 2012 3.
Reconveyance of the acquired land cannot be claimed as an absolute right.
An administrative decision by the Government is to be taken in this regard.
Lands were acquired for developing Tuticorin Port in the year 1964-65.
Award was passed in the year 1964 itself.
It is not in dispute that the compensation due were settled to the erstwhile land owners.
Once the lands are acquired, it absolutely vest with the Government and the title transfers to the Government and consequently the revenue records are also mutated.
4. Section 48(B) of the Land Acquisition Act is an enabling provision to take a decision by the Government.
However, on acquisition, title of the property is transferred in the name of the Government.
Thus, the erstwhile owners cannot seek reconveyance as a right.
With reference to the allegations of encroachment, the competent authority are bound to protect the Government land and utilise the same for public purposes.
In this regard, the authorities are obligated to initiate appropriate action to ensure that the lands are utilised for public purposes.
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis Review Application No.192 of 2012 5.

The petitioner himself admits that the lands covered under the Award No.6/64 and 9/64 were given possession to the Tuticorin Horbour Project but lands covered under Award No.31/65 were not given possession to the Tuticorin Port Project but retained by the State Government itself.
6. Once the lands are acquired, it is for the Government to take a decision to handover it to the requisitioning body or utilise the same for other public purposes.

Even if the lands are acquired for D.Thompson vs The Secretary To The Government on 10 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/86698281/
2 developing Tuticorin Horbour Project, the Government is empowered to utilise the land for other public purposes also.

sentences.text: Beyond all this, the application seeking reconveyance of land has been filed after a lapse of several years.
7. That being the legal position, reconveyance of land at this length of time cannot be sought for as a right.
More so, we are not called upon to decide the issues on merits since the writ petition and the writ appeal filed by the review petitioner are dismissed.
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis Review Application No.192 of 2012 8.
Since we do not find any error apparent on record to interfere with the order sought to be reviewed.
Thus, the present review petition stands dismissed.
No costs.

(S.M.S.J.,)
